newsitem.title: INDIA: India approved $4 bln foreign investment - minister.
newsitem.headline: India approved $4 bln foreign investment - minister.

text.p: India approved foreign direct investments of nearly $4 billion during the past two months, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Tuesday.

"During this short period, over 350 investment proposals, involving foreign direct investment of nearly $4 billion, have been approved by the government," Maran told a conference on foreign investment in India.

He said his ministry proposed to widen the number of industries eligible for automatic approval for foreign investors and to increase the equity ceiling for foreign investors in some high priority sectors.
"We are in the process of rationalising and expanding the list of high priority industries eligible for automatic approval," he said.
Currently India automatically approves foreign investment of up to 51 percent in 35 industries.
Maran told the conference that the ceiling for foreign equity would be raised for some high priority sectors.
"We also propose to raise the level of equity participation for some high priority items which would qualify for automatic approval."
The minister said the approval process had been streamlined with the aim of speeding up and widening the areas for foreign direct investment in India.
Foreign direct investment reached $2 billion in 1995, and the total inflow since 1991 has been around $5 billion.

The minister said the actual inflow of money from foreign direct investment was far below approved levels. "We are aware that the actual inflow of FDI (foreign direct investment) is 23 percent of total approvals," he said.
